questions.q: What is the biggest mistake to avoid when presenting this dashboard in the pricing review?
options: Walking through the visuals one by one, top to bottom, before stating what they mean
Using the slicer live during the conversation
Mentioning the out-of-scope items from Lesson 1
Formatting the measures before publishing
questions.explain: A visual-by-visual tour delays the actual answer; this lesson argues for stating the headline first, then supporting it with detail as needed.

questions.q: What should be said first, before pointing at any visual on the screen?
options: The headline answer to the original question, in one sentence
A description of how the T-SQL query was written
An apology for anything the report doesn't cover
A walkthrough of the slicer's options
questions.explain: Leading with the one-sentence answer respects the room's time and gives the detail a reason to matter when it follows.

questions.q: Why use the CategoryName slicer live during the presentation instead of just describing it?
options: Seeing the report respond to a click is more convincing than being told it can, especially when the conversation jumps between categories
The slicer cannot be demonstrated outside of Power BI Desktop
Describing the slicer verbally is required before using it
Live use of the slicer is the only way to trigger the DAX measures to calculate
questions.explain: A pricing review may naturally move between categories as different attendees ask about their own area, and showing the slicer respond live demonstrates the report's real value.

questions.q: What is the recommended response to a question the report wasn't scoped to answer, like a year-over-year comparison?
options: A short, honest statement that it's out of scope for this version, with an offer to add it as a follow-up
Guessing at an approximate answer based on general impressions
Explaining in detail why the comparison would be technically difficult to build
Declining to answer any further questions for the rest of the meeting
questions.explain: A brief, honest scoping response protects credibility and turns the gap into the start of a future iteration, rather than undermining the whole report.

questions.q: In the recommended three-beat structure, what comes right after the headline?
options: The "why" -- the bar chart, showing which categories are driving or dragging the headline number
The full detail table, narrated row by row
A description of the T-SQL query's JOIN structure
Opening the Power BI Service to show the published workspace
questions.explain: After the 10-15 second headline, the structure moves to the bar chart for 30-45 seconds to explain what's driving that headline, before the table is opened only if asked.
